Abdullah-Al-Mamun, learned Advocate, instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record.   ------ For the Petitioner

Zainul Abedin.  ------ Petitioner.
Vs.
The State ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim J: This Petition for Leave to Appeal at the instance the petitioner is directed against the judgment and order dated 06.04.2006 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.308 of 2006 filed under Section 561-A of the Code of Criminal Procedure discharging the Rule. 

 3. On receipt of the First Information Report the Police of Bancharampur Police Station recorded the case as Bancharampur Police Station Case No. 4 dated 20.09.2004 under Sections 6(1)/7/30 of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 corresponding to G.R. No. 7 of 2004 and then started investigation in the alleged allegation. 

 4. Mr. Abdullah-Al-Mamun, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner submits that the instant case arose out of kidnapping the victim, but the victim stated in her statements recorded under Section 22 of the said Ain that she was in a house wherein she was tortured for her activities as maid servant and thus the said sections will not lie against the petitioner in the instant case and as such the proceedings of the instant case is liable to be quashed; that the victim did not disclose the names of the petitioner in her such the judgment and order is liable to be set aside; that the victim was appointed as maid-servant in the house of the petitioner Nos. 4-5 for looking after a child and she was brought to the petitioner's house by the informant and as such the instant case is not maintainable under Section 7 of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 and thus the proceeding of the instant case is liable to be quashed; that the informant is the cousin of the victim and even the father and mother are not witnesses of the instant case and as such it is clear that the alleged occurrence did not happen in the alleged manner and place and as such the proceeding of the instant case is liable to be quashed; that the absence of any incriminating material against the petitioner, the proceeding's against the petitioner ought to be quashed to prevent the abuse of the process of Court and to secure the ends of justice; that the petitioner filed an application under Section 265(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the Tribunal who without perusing the papers and evidences on records rejected the said application and without explaining the cause of framing charge in his order dated 26.07.2005 passed an illegal order of framing charge without applying his judicial mind and as such the proceeding of the instant cases is liable to be quashed; that the alleged order of not discharging the petitioners got no legal basis and as such the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside for the ends of Justice. 

 5. It appears from the record that prima-facie allegation of offence under Section 7/30 of the said Ain was mentioned in F.I.R. and during investigation materials in support of the above allegation duly came forth and in statement under Section 22 of the Ain above allegation got further corroboration in specific manner. It manifestly appears that there is legal bar against continuation of the said proceeding. In the present case it obviously appears in F.I.R. that the prima-facie allegation about material as to the offence under Section 7/30 of the Ain were duly found mentioned and during investigation prima-facie materials in support of said offence duly came forth resulting in submission   of charge sheet and as such, there is no scope quashment of proceeding under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 6. In the case of Maudul Ahamed-vs-the State reported in 16 BLD (AD) 27 it was held that if prima-facie materials of the offence are disclosed in the case, there is no scope to seek quashment under Section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, whether the case is true or false will be only decided upon evidence at the trial.
